title: experiment-adaptive-batching-simulator
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: We wanted a lightweight, reproducible simulator to evaluate adaptive batching heuristics against realistic request arrival patterns without provisioning GPUs. This PR adds an experimental simulator and a small benchmark harness.

Summary: single-file simulator (python) plus workload generators and result visualization scripts. The simulator models worker pools, batch-formation delays, latency SLOs, and cost proxies. It is intentionally isolated under experimentation/ and is not wired into the serving runtime. Key outcomes included a ~12% estimated cost improvement on bursty workloads with minimal latency regressions in the 95th percentile for our synthetic traces.

How to run: python experiments/run_sim.py --workload traces/enterprise_bursty.json --policy adaptive_v1 --seed 42

Files added: experiments/run_sim.py, experiments/policies.py, experiments/workloads/ (sample traces), experiments/visualize.ipynb (exported html).

Notes: this is experimental code (no SLA). If we decide to promote parts into runtime, follow-up work must: (1) add thorough unit tests, (2) benchmark with real tokenization/model latency distributions, (3) design rollout policy and safety gates.

Checklist: [x] add simulator core [x] add two heuristic policies [x] include sample workloads [x] CI linting and basic unit tests [ ] add extended regression tests against recorded production traces

Related: ENG-9876 (linear), small prototype discussed in hackathon-2024 notes.
